title: How can we change a rectangle into a triangle of equal area?
description: The Shulba Sutras ask for a method to change a rectangle into a triangle with the same area. Extend the bottom side by its own length and join the new end to the top corner, and the triangle on the double base has the rectangle's area.
teaching_notes: One idea: a triangle on double the base with the same height has half of double the base times the height, which is the area of the rectangle. Watch for children who keep the same base and think the areas match.

video_script.why: The child uses half of base times height to see that a triangle needs double the base to match the area of a rectangle of the same height.
video_script.substitution: Double the base of the rectangle, keep its height, and join to make a triangle with half of double the base times the height.
video_script.anchor: the rectangle ABCD of the book, with its bottom side AB and its height AD
video_script.payoff_line: a triangle on double the base with the same height has the same area as the rectangle

maths_rules: rectangle ABCD with base AB and height AD; area = AB × AD
extend AB to E so that BE = AB, so AE = 2 × AB
join E to D; triangle AED has base AE = 2 × AB and height AD
area of triangle AED = 1/2 × 2AB × AD = AB × AD, which is the area of the rectangle
check with a rectangle 3 by 2: area 6; triangle with base 6 and height 2: 1/2 × 6 × 2 = 6
video_script.design: One idea: double the base to turn the rectangle into a triangle of equal area. The rectangle stays on stage; the new triangle grows from it. The check uses a rectangle three by two.
open_questions: The book figure is not in the extracted text. The worklist also gives another method (cut the rectangle along a diagonal and place the two halves side by side along the height); the video shows only the first method, which the question needs.
